+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Stream identity under the Confidential Computing copy patches.
+
+`torch.cuda.Stream()` hands out streams round-robin from a fixed pool of 32
+per device and priority. The CC patches key the event redirect on the raw
+handle of the D2H copy streams, so a pool stream taken later (e.g. by
+`graph_capture()` or an aux stream) must never share that handle: a capture
+would fail and a cross-stream join outside capture would be silently dropped.
+`new_d2h_stream()` therefore creates the copy streams outside the pool.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.distributed.device_communicators.cuda_wrapper import CudaRTLibrary
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.v1 import conf_compute_utils
+from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.async_utils import new_d2h_stream
+
+# Confidential Computing is NVIDIA-only: ROCm never takes these paths.
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not (current_platform.is_cuda() and torch.cuda.is_available()),
+    reason="needs NVIDIA CUDA",
+)
+
+POOL_WRAP = 64  # > 2 x the 32-stream pool, enough to see every pool handle
+

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Keep non-blocking host<->device copies non-blocking under NVIDIA CC.
+
+Under bounce-buffer Confidential Computing, cudaMemcpyAsync is
+host-synchronous: it returns only after the copy *and all prior work on its
+stream* complete. `install()` patches torch's non_blocking copy entry points
+so that:
+
+- H2D runs on an idle per-device staging stream, so the host waits only for
+  the transfer. The current stream then waits on the staging stream. A copy
+  into an existing tensor lands in a staging tensor and is moved by a D2D on
+  the current stream, so it is ordered exactly like the original copy. This
+  applies to every caller.
+- D2H issued on a stream created with `new_external_d2h_stream()` is issued
+  by a worker thread once the source is ready. Event / stream / device
+  synchronize additionally wait for the D2H copies submitted before the event
+  was recorded (or before the call). Using such a stream asserts that its D2H
+  sources aren't overwritten until the copy is synced (later compute-stream
+  work is never ordered after a side stream anyway), and that their completion
+  is only awaited through the patched torch.cuda / torch.Event methods. D2H on
+  any other stream keeps the original, host-blocking copy, since e.g. a
+  `torch.accelerator.current_stream().synchronize()` can't be patched.
+  A registered stream is only ever ordered after a producer stream by
+  `wait_stream()` and then carries D2H copies, so the events that mark its
+  position (the copies' readiness, and events recorded on it such as the
+  caller's copy event) are recorded on that producer stream instead. Under CC
+  an event recorded on an otherwise idle stream behind a cross-stream wait was
+  observed to fire only once the compute stream's *next* graph had finished,
+  which delayed every sampled token by a full step; an event recorded on the
+  producer stream fires on time.
+
+Copies made while torch.compile is tracing or a CUDA graph is being captured
+are left alone, as are H2D copies into an existing tensor that would need a
+staging buffer larger than `_MAX_STAGED_BYTES` (e.g. KV cache swaps).
+"""
+
+import threading
+import weakref
+from concurrent.futures import Future, ThreadPoolExecutor
+from functools import cache
+from typing import Any
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+_orig_copy_ = torch.Tensor.copy_
+_orig_to = torch.Tensor.to
+_orig_cuda = torch.Tensor.cuda
+_orig_event_cls = torch.Event
+# The torch.cuda originals are captured by install(): CPU-only torch builds
+# ship a placeholder torch.cuda.Event/Stream without these methods, and this
+# module is imported by the GPU model runner on every platform.
+_orig_cuda_event_record: Any = None
+_orig_cuda_event_synchronize: Any = None
+_orig_stream_synchronize: Any = None
+_orig_stream_wait_stream: Any = None
+_orig_stream_query: Any = None
+_orig_cuda_synchronize: Any = None
+_orig_accel_synchronize: Any = None
+
+# Single worker keeps D2H copies in submission order; created by install().
+_d2h_executor: ThreadPoolExecutor | None = None
+_pending_lock = threading.Lock()
+_pending: list[Future] = []
+# Raw handles of the streams created via new_external_d2h_stream().
+_d2h_streams: set[int] = set()
+# For each registered stream, the producer stream it last waited on.
+_producer_of: dict[int, torch.cuda.Stream] = {}
+# Storage base addresses of the tensors registered via
+# register_inplace_h2d_target(); views of them are matched too.
+_inplace_h2d_storages: set[int] = set()
+# Upper bound on the staging buffer an H2D copy into an existing tensor may use.
+_MAX_STAGED_BYTES = 32 << 20
+
+
+_CUDA_STREAM_NON_BLOCKING = 0x01
+
+
+def _new_external_stream(device: torch.device) -> torch.cuda.Stream:
+    """A stream created outside torch's per-device pool, so `torch.cuda.Stream()`
+    can never hand out its handle again (the pool is 32 streams, round-robin)."""
+    from vllm.distributed.device_communicators.cuda_wrapper import CudaRTLibrary
+
+    with torch.cuda.device(device):
+        handle = CudaRTLibrary().cudaStreamCreateWithFlags(_CUDA_STREAM_NON_BLOCKING)
+    return torch.cuda.ExternalStream(handle, device=device)
+
+
+def new_external_d2h_stream(
+    device: torch.device | int | None = None,
+) -> torch.cuda.Stream:
+    """Create a stream whose non_blocking D2H copies go through the worker
+    thread once `install()` has run (see the module docstring). Callers use
+    this through `async_utils.new_d2h_stream()`.
+
+    The stream is created outside torch's stream pool: the patches key on the
+    raw handle, and a pool stream handed out later (e.g. by `graph_capture()`
+    or `aux_stream()`) must never share it, or its events would be redirected
+    to the producer stream. The stream lives for the life of the process.
+
+    Such a stream must only carry copies: readiness is tracked on the stream
+    it last waited on via `wait_stream()`, so a kernel launched on the copy
+    stream itself is not ordered before the copies of its output. Compute such
+    values on the producer stream first.
+    """
+    dev = torch.device("cuda") if device is None else torch.device(device)
+    if dev.index is None:
+        dev = torch.device("cuda", torch.cuda.current_device())
+    stream = _new_external_stream(dev)
+    assert stream.cuda_stream not in _d2h_streams, "duplicate D2H stream handle"
+    _d2h_streams.add(stream.cuda_stream)
+    return stream
+
+
+def register_inplace_h2d_target(tensor: torch.Tensor) -> None:
+    """Let non_blocking H2D copies into `tensor` (or a view of it) land in
+    place on the staging stream once `install()` has run: no staging tensor
+    and no D2D. The caller guarantees that no GPU reader of `tensor` is still
+    in flight whenever it is rewritten (e.g. a round-robin pool slot whose
+    readers retired). The staging stream is ordered once after the current
+    stream, so work that initialized `tensor` (e.g. the zero fill of a fresh
+    allocation) completes before the first in-place upload. The registration
+    lapses with `tensor`, so a later tensor reusing its memory is not matched.
+    """
+    from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+    if not tensor.is_cuda or not current_platform.is_confidential_compute():
+        return
+    ptr = tensor.untyped_storage().data_ptr()
+    cur = torch.cuda.current_stream(tensor.device)
+    _staging_stream(cur.device_index).wait_stream(cur)
+    _inplace_h2d_storages.add(ptr)
+    weakref.finalize(tensor, _inplace_h2d_storages.discard, ptr)
+
+
+@cache
+def _staging_stream(device_index: int) -> torch.cuda.Stream:
+    return _new_external_stream(torch.device("cuda", device_index))
+
+
+@cache
+def _d2h_stream(device_index: int) -> torch.cuda.Stream:
+    return _new_external_stream(torch.device("cuda", device_index))
+
+
+def _nbytes(t: torch.Tensor) -> int:
+    return t.numel() * t.element_size()
+
+
+def _bypass() -> bool:
+    return torch.compiler.is_compiling() or torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()
+
+
+def _h2d(
+    src: torch.Tensor,
+    device: torch.device,
+    dtype: torch.dtype | None = None,
+    out: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    cur = torch.cuda.current_stream(device)
+    staging = _staging_stream(cur.device_index)
+    with torch.cuda.stream(staging):
+        tmp = _orig_to(src, device=cur.device, dtype=dtype, non_blocking=True)
+    cur.wait_stream(staging)
+    tmp.record_stream(cur)
+    return tmp if out is None else _orig_copy_(out, tmp, non_blocking=True)
+
+
+def _h2d_inplace(out: torch.Tensor, src: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    cur = torch.cuda.current_stream(out.device)
+    staging = _staging_stream(cur.device_index)
+    with torch.cuda.stream(staging):
+        _orig_copy_(out, src, non_blocking=True)
+    cur.wait_stream(staging)
+    return out
+
+
+def _d2h(src: torch.Tensor, out: torch.Tensor | None = None) -> torch.Tensor | None:
+    """Returns None if the copy should fall back to the original method."""
+    cur = torch.cuda.current_stream(src.device)
+    if cur.cuda_stream not in _d2h_streams:
+        return None
+    if out is None:
+        out = torch.empty(src.shape, dtype=src.dtype, pin_memory=True)
+    ready = torch.cuda.Event(blocking=True)
+    _orig_cuda_event_record(ready, _producer_of.get(cur.cuda_stream, cur))
+
+    def run() -> None:
+        # Sleep until the producer is done, so the host-synchronous copy only
+        # pays for its own transfer (and doesn't hold driver locks meanwhile).
+        _orig_cuda_event_synchronize(ready)
+        side = _d2h_stream(src.device.index)
+        # Entering the stream also switches this thread to its device.
+        # Inference mode is thread-local, and out may be an inference tensor;
+        # an in-place copy into a normal tensor is allowed in inference mode.
+        with torch.inference_mode(), torch.cuda.stream(side):
+            _orig_copy_(out, src, non_blocking=True)
+            # The closure keeps src alive until here; this keeps the caching
+            # allocator from reusing it before the copy has run.
+            src.record_stream(side)
+        _orig_stream_synchronize(side)
+
+    assert _d2h_executor is not None
+    fut = _d2h_executor.submit(run)
+    with _pending_lock:
+        _pending.append(fut)
+    return out
+
+
+def _pending_snapshot() -> list[Future]:
+    with _pending_lock:
+        _pending[:] = [f for f in _pending if not f.done()]
+        return list(_pending)
+
+
+def _wait_pending() -> None:
+    for f in _pending_snapshot():
+        f.result()
+
+
+def _copy_(self: torch.Tensor, src: torch.Tensor, non_blocking: bool = False):
+    if non_blocking and not _bypass():
+        if self.is_cuda and src.is_cpu:
+            if (
+                _inplace_h2d_storages
+                and self.dtype == src.dtype
+                and self.untyped_storage().data_ptr() in _inplace_h2d_storages
+            ):
+                return _h2d_inplace(self, src)
+            if _nbytes(src) <= _MAX_STAGED_BYTES:
+                return _h2d(src, self.device, out=self)
+        if (
+            self.is_cpu
+            and src.is_cuda
+            and self.shape == src.shape
+            and self.dtype == src.dtype
+            and (out := _d2h(src, out=self)) is not None
+        ):
+            return out
+    return _orig_copy_(self, src, non_blocking)
+
+
+def _to(self: torch.Tensor, *args, **kwargs):
+    if not (kwargs.get("non_blocking") or any(a is True for a in args)) or _bypass():
+        return _orig_to(self, *args, **kwargs)
+    parse_kwargs = {k: v for k, v in kwargs.items() if k != "copy"}
+    device, dtype, _, memory_format = torch._C._nn._parse_to(*args, **parse_kwargs)
+    if device is not None and memory_format is None:
+        if self.is_cpu and device.type == "cuda":
+            return _h2d(self, device, dtype)
+        if (
+            self.is_cuda
+            and device.type == "cpu"
+            and dtype in (None, self.dtype)
+            and (out := _d2h(self)) is not None
+        ):
+            return out
+    return _orig_to(self, *args, **kwargs)
+
+
+def _cuda(
+    self: torch.Tensor,
+    device=None,
+    non_blocking: bool = False,
+    memory_format: torch.memory_format = torch.preserve_format,
+):
+    if (
+        non_blocking
+        and self.is_cpu
+        and memory_format == torch.preserve_format
+        and not _bypass()
+    ):
+        if device is None:
+            device = torch.accelerator.current_device_index()
+        if isinstance(device, int):
+            device = torch.device("cuda", device)
+        return _h2d(self, torch.device(device))
+    return _orig_cuda(self, device, non_blocking, memory_format)
+
+
+def _patch_event_methods(cls: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Wrap `cls`'s record/synchronize/query so a recorded event also covers
+    the D2H copies submitted before it was recorded."""
+    orig_record, orig_synchronize, orig_query = (
+        cls.record,
+        cls.synchronize,
+        cls.query,
+    )
+
+    def record(self, stream=None):
+        self._cc_pending = _pending_snapshot()
+        stream = _record_target(stream)
+        if stream is None:
+            return orig_record(self)
+        return orig_record(self, stream)
+
+    def synchronize(self):
+        for f in getattr(self, "_cc_pending", ()):
+            f.result()
+        return orig_synchronize(self)
+
+    def query(self):
+        pending = getattr(self, "_cc_pending", ())

+def test_stashed_logprobs_match_compute_topk_scores(
+    num_logprobs: int, with_ids: bool, logits_mode: bool, dtype: torch.dtype
+):
+    """The stash kernels report what compute_topk_scores reports for the
+    scaled rows and touch only the converged slots' real rows. Which tied id
+    makes a top-k cutoff is not guaranteed by either side, so the top-k ids
+    are compared by the values they hold, and as a set only where the cutoff
+    is not tied."""
+    set_random_seed(0)
+    # A row spans several kernel chunks of 16 * 1024 logits.
+    n, W, vocab, max_reqs, cl = 5, 4, 40001, 8, 6
+    tile = (torch.randn(n * W, vocab, device="cuda") * 3).to(dtype)
+    # 129 distinct maxima, exact in bf16: every top-k cutoff is clear.
+    tile[0, 300:39000:300] = 16 + 0.5 * torch.arange(129, device="cuda")
+    # A max tied across chunks: the argmax is the first, the rank counts both.
+    tile[1, [7, 39000]] = 20.0
+    # A max tied 201 times across chunks straddles every top-k cutoff.
+    tile[2, ::200] = 25.0
+    # A row top_k left 3 logits of: the rest of its top-k ties at -inf.
+    tile[3 * W] = float("-inf")
+    tile[3 * W, [5, 17000, 40000]] = 1.0
+    local = torch.tensor([0, 2, 3], device="cuda")  # requests that want logprobs
+    slots = torch.tensor([6, 1, 4], device="cuda")
+    keep = torch.tensor([True, False, True], device="cuda")
+    temps = torch.tensor([0.7, 1.0, 1.3], device="cuda")
+    # The last request's canvas is truncated: its last row is padding.
+    valid = torch.tensor([W, W, W - 1], device="cuda")
+
+    ids_state = LogprobTokenIdsState(max_reqs, torch.device("cuda"))
+    if with_ids:
+        ids_state.add_request(4, SamplingParams(logprob_token_ids=[3, 5, 8000]))
+        ids_state.apply_staged_writes()
+    max_ids = 3 if with_ids else 0
+
+    scaled = tile.view(n, W, vocab)[local].float() / temps[:, None, None]
+    scaled = scaled.view(-1, vocab)
+    ref = compute_topk_scores(
+        scaled,
+        num_logprobs,
+        scaled.argmax(dim=-1),
+        logprob_token_ids_state=ids_state if with_ids else None,
+        expanded_idx_mapping=(
+            slots.to(torch.int32).repeat_interleave(W) if with_ids else None
+        ),
+        max_per_req_token_ids=max_ids,
+        logits_mode=logits_mode,
+    )
+
+    stash_w = 1 + max(num_logprobs, max_ids) + 2
+    stash_ids = torch.full((max_reqs, cl, stash_w), 77, device="cuda")
+    stash_lps = torch.ones(max_reqs, cl, stash_w, device="cuda")
+    stash_ranks = torch.full((max_reqs, cl), 99, device="cuda")
+    stash_converged_logprobs(

+        W,
+        local,
+        slots,
+        keep,
+        valid,
+        temps,
+        num_logprobs,
+        ids_state.num_token_ids.gpu,
+        ids_state.token_ids.gpu if with_ids else None,
+        stash_ids,
+        stash_lps,
+        stash_ranks,
+        logits_mode,
+    )
+
+    width = ref.logprobs.shape[1]
+    for j, slot in enumerate(slots.tolist()):
+        v = int(valid[j])
+        rows = slice(j * W, j * W + v)
+        if not keep[j]:
+            assert (stash_ids[slot] == 77).all() and (stash_ranks[slot] == 99).all()

+        # the argmax and rank match exactly; the logsumexp is a float reduction.

+        assert torch.equal(ids[:, 0], ref.logprob_token_ids[rows, 0])
+        held, ref_ids = scaled[rows], ref.logprob_token_ids[rows]
+        assert torch.equal(held.gather(1, ids), held.gather(1, ref_ids))
+        if with_ids and slot == 4:

+        elif num_logprobs:
+            top = held.topk(num_logprobs + 1, dim=-1).values
+            untied = top[:, -2] > top[:, -1]

+        assert not stash_ids[slot, :v, width:].any()
+        assert torch.isneginf(stash_lps[slot, :v, width:]).all()
+        # Padding rows and positions past this tile's width are left alone.
+        assert (stash_ranks[slot, v:] == 99).all()

+    order-preserving int32 in the high word, the inverted index in the low.
+    Keys are distinct, so the top-k under them is unique.
+    """
+    j = tl.program_id(0)
+    pos = tl.program_id(1)
+    chunk = tl.program_id(2)
+    if _lp_skip_topk(keep_ptr, valid_ptr, slots_ptr, num_ids_ptr, j, pos, HAS_IDS):
+        return
+    r = (j * W + pos).to(tl.int64)
+    # K block maxima are K distinct elements at or above the K-th largest
+    # block max, so every top-k element is too: the rest of the row is
+    # skipped without a reduction over it.
+    b = tl.arange(0, BLOCKS_POW2)
+    block_max = tl.load(
+        block_max_ptr + r * NUM_BLOCKS + b, mask=b < NUM_BLOCKS, other=float("-inf")
+    )
+    sorted_max = tl.sort(_lp_key32(block_max), descending=True)
+    kth = tl.max(tl.where(b == K - 1, sorted_max, -0x7FFFFFFF - 1), 0)
+    threshold = kth.to(tl.int64) << 32
+    # Distinct placeholders below every real key.
+    best = _NO_KEY + 1 + tl.arange(0, KP).to(tl.int64)
+    best_min = tl.min(best, 0)
+    for blk in range(BLOCKS_PER_CHUNK):
+        offs = (chunk * BLOCKS_PER_CHUNK + blk) * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+        x = _lp_load(
+            logits_ptr,
+            logits_stride,
+            src_ptr,
+            temps_ptr,
+            j,
+            pos,
+            W,
+            offs,
+            V,
+            float("-inf"),
+        )
+        key = (_lp_key32(x).to(tl.int64) << 32) | (0x7FFFFFFF - offs).to(tl.int64)
+        key = tl.where((offs < V) & (key >= threshold), key, _NO_KEY)
+        key_max = tl.max(key, 0)
+        while key_max > best_min:
+            best = tl.where(best == best_min, key_max, best)
+            best_min = tl.min(best, 0)
+            key = tl.where(key == key_max, _NO_KEY, key)
+            key_max = tl.max(key, 0)
+    out = (r * NUM_CHUNKS + chunk) * KP + tl.arange(0, KP)
+    tl.store(cand_ptr + out, best)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _lp_topk_merge_kernel(
+    keep_ptr,
+    valid_ptr,
+    slots_ptr,
+    num_ids_ptr,
+    cand_ptr,
+    topk_ptr,
+    K,
+    W,
+    NUM_CAND,
+    HAS_IDS: tl.constexpr,
+    CAND_POW2: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    j = tl.program_id(0)
+    pos = tl.program_id(1)
+    if _lp_skip_topk(keep_ptr, valid_ptr, slots_ptr, num_ids_ptr, j, pos, HAS_IDS):
+        return
+    r = (j * W + pos).to(tl.int64)
+    c = tl.arange(0, CAND_POW2)
+    keys = tl.load(cand_ptr + r * NUM_CAND + c, mask=c < NUM_CAND, other=_NO_KEY)
+    keys = tl.sort(keys, descending=True)
+    ids = 0x7FFFFFFF - (keys & 0x7FFFFFFF)
+    tl.store(topk_ptr + r * K + c, ids.to(tl.int32), mask=c < K)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _lp_write_kernel(
+    logits_ptr,
+    logits_stride,
+    src_ptr,
+    slots_ptr,
+    keep_ptr,
+    valid_ptr,
+    temps_ptr,
+    chunk_max_ptr,
+    chunk_arg_ptr,
+    block_sum_ptr,
+    block_cnt_ptr,
+    topk_ptr,
+    num_ids_ptr,
+    ids_ptr,
+    ids_stride,
+    out_ids_ptr,
+    out_lp_ptr,
+    out_rank_ptr,
+    num_topk,
+    W,
+    CL,
+    V,
+    STASH_W,
+    NUM_CHUNKS,
+    NUM_BLOCKS,
+    HAS_IDS: tl.constexpr,
+    LOGITS_MODE: tl.constexpr,
+    CHUNKS_POW2: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCKS_POW2: tl.constexpr,
+    SUM_GROUP: tl.constexpr,
+    COL_BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    j = tl.program_id(0)
+    pos = tl.program_id(1)
+    if _lp_skip(keep_ptr, valid_ptr, j, pos):
+        return
+    r = (j * W + pos).to(tl.int64)
+    c = tl.arange(0, CHUNKS_POW2)
+    in_chunks = c < NUM_CHUNKS
+    maxes = tl.load(
+        chunk_max_ptr + r * NUM_CHUNKS + c, mask=in_chunks, other=float("-inf")
+    )
+    max_val = tl.max(maxes, 0)
+    # The first chunk holding the max holds the first-index argmax.
+    first = tl.min(tl.where(maxes == max_val, c, CHUNKS_POW2), 0)
+    best_idx = tl.load(chunk_arg_ptr + r * NUM_CHUNKS + first).to(tl.int64)
+    blocks = tl.arange(0, BLOCKS_POW2)
+    rank = tl.sum(
+        tl.load(block_cnt_ptr + r * NUM_BLOCKS + blocks, mask=blocks < NUM_BLOCKS)
+    )
+    # Add the block sums one by one in block order. A group is loaded at once
+    # and each sum picked out by a masked sum, which adds only zeros to it, so
+    # the loop does not wait on a load per block.
+    lanes = tl.arange(0, SUM_GROUP)
+    se = 0.0
+    for g in range(0, NUM_BLOCKS, SUM_GROUP):
+        sums = tl.load(
+            block_sum_ptr + r * NUM_BLOCKS + g + lanes,
+            mask=g + lanes < NUM_BLOCKS,
+            other=0.0,
+        )
+        for i in tl.static_range(SUM_GROUP):
+            se += tl.sum(tl.where(lanes == i, sums, 0.0))
+    lse = tl.log(se)
+
+    row = (tl.load(src_ptr + j) * W + pos).to(tl.int64)
+    base = logits_ptr + row * logits_stride
+    temp = tl.load(temps_ptr + j)
+    slot = tl.load(slots_ptr + j).to(tl.int64)
+    out = (slot * CL + pos) * STASH_W
+    tl.store(out_rank_ptr + slot * CL + pos, rank)
+    num_ids = 0
+    if HAS_IDS:
+        num_ids = tl.load(num_ids_ptr + slot)
+    for c0 in range(0, STASH_W, COL_BLOCK):
+        col = c0 + tl.arange(0, COL_BLOCK)
+        k = col - 1
+        # Column 0 is the argmax; then the request's own token ids, or else
+        # the top-k. The rest pads with token 0 at -inf.
+        in_topk = (k >= 0) & (k < num_topk) & (num_ids == 0)
+        tok = tl.load(topk_ptr + r * num_topk + k, mask=in_topk, other=0)
+        tok = tok.to(tl.int64)
+        valid = (col == 0) | in_topk
+        if HAS_IDS:
+            in_ids = (k >= 0) & (k < num_ids)
+            from_ids = tl.load(ids_ptr + slot * ids_stride + k, mask=in_ids, other=0)
+            tok = tl.where(in_ids, from_ids.to(tl.int64), tok)
+            valid = valid | in_ids
+        tok = tl.where(col == 0, best_idx, tok)
+        x = tl.load(base + tok, mask=valid, other=0.0).to(tl.float32)
+        x = tl.div_rn(x, temp)
+        if not LOGITS_MODE:
+            x = x - max_val - lse
+        in_stash = col < STASH_W
+        tl.store(out_ids_ptr + out + col, tl.where(valid, tok, 0), mask=in_stash)
+        tl.store(
+            out_lp_ptr + out + col, tl.where(valid, x, float("-inf")), mask=in_stash
+        )
+
+
+def stash_converged_logprobs(
+    logits: torch.Tensor,
+    canvas_len: int,
+    src: torch.Tensor,
+    slots: torch.Tensor,
+    keep: torch.Tensor,
+    valid: torch.Tensor,
+    temps: torch.Tensor,
+    num_topk: int,
+    num_token_ids: torch.Tensor,
+    token_ids: torch.Tensor | None,
+    out_ids: torch.Tensor,
+    out_logprobs: torch.Tensor,
+    out_ranks: torch.Tensor,
+    logits_mode: bool,
+) -> None:
+    """Write the logprobs of the converged requests' rows to the stash.
+
+    Request `j` owns logits rows `src[j] * canvas_len + p` for
+    `p < valid[j]`, divided by `temps[j]`. Where `keep[j]`, they go to
+    `out_*[slots[j], p]`, laid out as compute_topk_scores lays out a row:
+    the argmax, then the request's `token_ids` if it has any, else the
+    `num_topk` largest (tied ids by lower id), padded with token 0 at -inf.
+    Rows not kept exit at once; the others are split into chunks so a few
+    kept rows still fill the GPU.
+    """
+    m = slots.shape[0]
+    vocab = logits.shape[-1]
+    assert logits.stride(-1) == 1
+    assert temps.dtype == torch.float32
+    assert num_topk + 1 <= out_logprobs.shape[-1]
+    block = _LP_BLOCK
+    num_blocks = triton.cdiv(vocab, block)
+    blocks_per_chunk = min(_LP_BLOCKS_PER_CHUNK, num_blocks)
+    num_chunks = triton.cdiv(num_blocks, blocks_per_chunk)
+    rows = m * canvas_len
+    device = logits.device
+    chunk_max = torch.empty(rows, num_chunks, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
+    chunk_arg = torch.empty(rows, num_chunks, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
+    block_sum = torch.empty(rows, num_blocks, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
+    block_cnt = torch.empty(rows, num_blocks, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    block_max = (
+        torch.empty(rows, num_blocks, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
+        if num_topk > 0
+        else chunk_max
+    )
+    has_ids = token_ids is not None
+    ids_arg = token_ids if token_ids is not None else num_token_ids
+    common = (logits, logits.stride(0), src, keep, valid, temps)
+    grid = (m, canvas_len, num_chunks)
+    _lp_max_kernel[grid](
+        *common,
+        chunk_max,
+        chunk_arg,
+        block_max,
+        canvas_len,
+        vocab,
+        num_chunks,
+        num_blocks,
+        BLOCK=block,
+        BLOCKS_PER_CHUNK=blocks_per_chunk,
+        STORE_BLOCK_MAX=num_topk > 0,
+        num_warps=4,
+    )
+    chunks_pow2 = triton.next_power_of_2(num_chunks)
+    _lp_sum_kernel[grid](
+        *common,
+        chunk_max,
+        block_sum,
+        block_cnt,
+        canvas_len,
+        vocab,
+        num_chunks,
+        num_blocks,
+        BLOCK=block,
+        BLOCKS_PER_CHUNK=blocks_per_chunk,
+        CHUNKS_POW2=chunks_pow2,
+        num_warps=4,
+    )
+    topk = chunk_arg
+    if num_topk > 0:
+        kp = triton.next_power_of_2(num_topk)
+        cand = torch.empty(rows, num_chunks, kp, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
+        _lp_topk_kernel[grid](
+            *common,
+            slots,
+            num_token_ids,
+            block_max,
+            cand,
+            num_topk,
+            canvas_len,
+            vocab,
+            num_chunks,
+            num_blocks,
+            HAS_IDS=has_ids,
+            BLOCK=block,
+            BLOCKS_PER_CHUNK=blocks_per_chunk,
+            BLOCKS_POW2=triton.next_power_of_2(max(num_blocks, num_topk)),
+            KP=kp,
+            num_warps=4,
+        )
+        topk = torch.empty(rows, num_topk, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+        _lp_topk_merge_kernel[(m, canvas_len)](
+            keep,
+            valid,
+            slots,
+            num_token_ids,
+            cand,
+            topk,
+            num_topk,
+            canvas_len,
+            num_chunks * kp,
+            HAS_IDS=has_ids,
+            CAND_POW2=triton.next_power_of_2(num_chunks * kp),
+        )
+    stash_width = out_logprobs.shape[-1]
+    _lp_write_kernel[(m, canvas_len)](
+        logits,
+        logits.stride(0),
+        src,
+        slots,
+        keep,
+        valid,
+        temps,
+        chunk_max,
+        chunk_arg,
+        block_sum,
+        block_cnt,
+        topk,
+        num_token_ids,
+        ids_arg,
+        ids_arg.stride(0) if has_ids else 0,
+        out_ids,
+        out_logprobs,
+        out_ranks,
+        num_topk,
+        canvas_len,
+        out_logprobs.shape[1],
+        vocab,
+        stash_width,
+        num_chunks,
+        num_blocks,
+        HAS_IDS=has_ids,
+        LOGITS_MODE=logits_mode,
+        CHUNKS_POW2=chunks_pow2,
+        BLOCKS_POW2=triton.next_power_of_2(num_blocks),
+        SUM_GROUP=16,
+        COL_BLOCK=min(triton.next_power_of_2(stash_width), 1024),
+    )

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+
+"""How the AsyncLLM output handler reports an engine core that is already gone."""
+
+import asyncio
+import time
+
+import pytest
+
+from vllm.config import KernelConfig
+from vllm.engine.arg_utils import AsyncEngineArgs
+from vllm.outputs import RequestOutput
+from vllm.sampling_params import RequestOutputKind, SamplingParams
+from vllm.v1.engine import async_llm as async_llm_module
+from vllm.v1.engine.async_llm import AsyncLLM
+from vllm.v1.engine.exceptions import EngineDeadError
+
+MODEL = "hmellor/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM"
+TIMEOUT_SEC = 30
+FAILURE_LOG = "AsyncLLM output_handler failed."
+STOP_LOG = "Engine core gone during shutdown; output handler exiting"
+
+
+def _make_engine() -> AsyncLLM:
+    return AsyncLLM.from_engine_args(
+        AsyncEngineArgs(
+            model=MODEL,
+            enforce_eager=True,
+            kernel_config=KernelConfig(enable_jit_warmup=False),
+        )
+    )
+
+
+async def _start_long_request(engine: AsyncLLM) -> asyncio.Task:
+    """Start a request, returning once it is streaming, that outlives the test."""
+    stream = engine.generate(
+        "Hello my name is",
+        request_id="in-flight",
+        sampling_params=SamplingParams(
+            max_tokens=2000,
+            ignore_eos=True,
+            output_kind=RequestOutputKind.DELTA,
+        ),
+    )
+    last_output = await anext(stream)
+
+    async def drain() -> RequestOutput:
+        nonlocal last_output
+        async for output in stream:
+            last_output = output
+        return last_output
+
+    return asyncio.create_task(drain())
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_requested_stop_is_not_reported_as_a_failure(caplog_vllm, monkeypatch):
+    real_cancel = async_llm_module.cancel_task_threadsafe
+
+    def cancel_after_handler_exits(task: asyncio.Task) -> None:
+        # Force the race: the handler sees the stopped core before its cancel.
+        deadline = time.monotonic() + TIMEOUT_SEC
+        while not task.done() and time.monotonic() < deadline:
+            time.sleep(0.01)
+        assert task.done()
+        real_cancel(task)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        async_llm_module, "cancel_task_threadsafe", cancel_after_handler_exits
+    )
+
+    engine = _make_engine()
+    try:
+        request = await _start_long_request(engine)
+        await asyncio.get_running_loop().run_in_executor(None, engine.shutdown)
+    finally:
+        engine.shutdown()
+
+    assert FAILURE_LOG not in caplog_vllm.text
+    assert STOP_LOG in caplog_vllm.text
+    # The request must end, not hang: finished by the core's abort, or failed.
+    [outcome] = await asyncio.wait_for(
+        asyncio.gather(request, return_exceptions=True), TIMEOUT_SEC
+    )
+    if isinstance(outcome, BaseException):
+        assert isinstance(outcome, EngineDeadError)
+    else:
+        assert outcome.finished
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_death_outside_shutdown_is_still_reported(caplog_vllm):
+    engine = _make_engine()
+    try:
+        request = await _start_long_request(engine)
+        engine.engine_core.resources.engine_manager.processes[0].kill()
+        with pytest.raises(EngineDeadError):
+            await asyncio.wait_for(request, TIMEOUT_SEC)
+        assert engine.output_handler is not None
+        await asyncio.wait_for(engine.output_handler, TIMEOUT_SEC)
+    finally:
+        engine.shutdown()
+
+    assert FAILURE_LOG in caplog_vllm.text
+    assert STOP_LOG not in caplog_vllm.text

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Correctness tests for the AMD Qwen4Exp hyper-connection kernels."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+
+from vllm.models.qwen4_exp.amd.ops.hc import (
+    grouped_gemma_rmsnorm,
+    hc_combine,
+    hc_combine_norm,
+    hc_gate_mix,
+    hc_silu,
+)
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.triton_utils import HAS_TRITON
+from vllm.utils.torch_utils import set_random_seed
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not current_platform.is_rocm() or not HAS_TRITON,
+    reason="AMD HC kernels require ROCm and Triton",
+)
+
+HC = 4
+HIDDEN_SIZE = 2560
+HYPER_HIDDEN_SIZE = HC * HIDDEN_SIZE
+EPS = 1e-6
+LORA_RANK = 320
+DOWN_N = LORA_RANK + HC + 12  # merged down+inject weight, 16-row padded
+NUM_TOKENS = [1, 17, 2048]
+# A [HIDDEN_SIZE] norm weight is shared by all streams; a [HYPER_HIDDEN_SIZE]
+# one is per branch (hc_per_branch_norm).
+NORM_SIZES = [HIDDEN_SIZE, HYPER_HIDDEN_SIZE]
+
+
+def _randn(*shape: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    return torch.randn(*shape, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+
+
+def _ref_grouped_gemma_rmsnorm(x: torch.Tensor, weight: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    grouped = x.float().unflatten(-1, (HC, HIDDEN_SIZE))
+    variance = grouped.square().mean(-1, keepdim=True)
+    normed = grouped * torch.rsqrt(variance + EPS)
+    weight = weight.float().reshape(-1, HIDDEN_SIZE)
+    return (normed * (1.0 + weight)).flatten(-2).to(torch.bfloat16)
+
+
+def _ref_hc_combine(
+    residual: torch.Tensor, block_output: torch.Tensor, injection: torch.Tensor
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    injection_weight = 2.0 * torch.sigmoid(injection.float() / HC)
+    expected = residual.float().unflatten(-1, (HC, HIDDEN_SIZE))
+    expected = expected + block_output.float().unsqueeze(
+        -2
+    ) * injection_weight.unsqueeze(-1)
+    return expected.flatten(-2).to(torch.bfloat16)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("norm_size", NORM_SIZES)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_tokens", NUM_TOKENS)
+def test_grouped_gemma_rmsnorm(num_tokens: int, norm_size: int) -> None:
+    set_random_seed(0)
+    x = _randn(num_tokens, HYPER_HIDDEN_SIZE)
+    weight = _randn(norm_size)
+
+    actual = grouped_gemma_rmsnorm(x, weight, EPS, HC)
+
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, _ref_grouped_gemma_rmsnorm(x, weight))
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_tokens", NUM_TOKENS)
+def test_hc_silu(num_tokens: int) -> None:
+    # lowrank is a column slice of the merged down+inject output, as in the model.
+    set_random_seed(0)
+    lowrank = _randn(num_tokens, DOWN_N)[:, :LORA_RANK]
+
+    actual = hc_silu(lowrank, HC)
+
+    expected = F.silu(lowrank.float() / HC).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_tokens", NUM_TOKENS)
+def test_hc_gate_mix(num_tokens: int) -> None:
+    set_random_seed(0)
+    x = _randn(num_tokens, HYPER_HIDDEN_SIZE)
+    gate = _randn(num_tokens, HYPER_HIDDEN_SIZE)
+
+    actual = hc_gate_mix(x, gate, HC)
+    expected = (
+        torch.sigmoid(gate.float().unflatten(-1, (HC, HIDDEN_SIZE)))
+        * x.float().unflatten(-1, (HC, HIDDEN_SIZE))
+    ).mean(-2)
+
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected.to(torch.bfloat16))
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_tokens", NUM_TOKENS)
+def test_hc_combine(num_tokens: int) -> None:
+    # injection is a column slice of the merged down+inject output, as in the model.
+    set_random_seed(0)
+    block_output = _randn(num_tokens, HIDDEN_SIZE)
+    residual = _randn(num_tokens, HYPER_HIDDEN_SIZE)
+    injection = _randn(num_tokens, DOWN_N)[:, LORA_RANK : LORA_RANK + HC]
+
+    actual = hc_combine(residual, block_output, injection, HC)
+
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        actual, _ref_hc_combine(residual, block_output, injection)
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("norm_size", NORM_SIZES)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_tokens", NUM_TOKENS)
+def test_hc_combine_norm(num_tokens: int, norm_size: int) -> None:
+    set_random_seed(0)
+    block_output = _randn(num_tokens, HIDDEN_SIZE)
+    residual = _randn(num_tokens, HYPER_HIDDEN_SIZE)
+    injection = _randn(num_tokens, DOWN_N)[:, LORA_RANK : LORA_RANK + HC]
+    weight = _randn(norm_size)
+
+    actual, actual_norm = hc_combine_norm(
+        residual, block_output, injection, weight, EPS, HC
+    )
+
+    expected = _ref_hc_combine(residual, block_output, injection)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        actual_norm, _ref_grouped_gemma_rmsnorm(expected, weight)
+    )

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

+
+import pytest
+import requests
+
+from tests.models.language.pooling.embed_utils import float_embeddings
+from tests.models.utils import check_embeddings_close
+from tests.utils import RemoteOpenAIServer
+from vllm.entrypoints.pooling.embed.protocol import EmbeddingResponse
+from vllm.multimodal.utils import encode_image_url, fetch_image
+
+image_url = "https://vllm-public-assets.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/multimodal_asset/cat_snow.jpg"
+image_base64 = {"url": encode_image_url(fetch_image(image_url))}
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "dual_encoder_model",
+    ["openai/clip-vit-base-patch32", "google/siglip-base-patch16-224"],
+)
+def test_dual_encoder_chat_text_matches_input(dual_encoder_model: str):
+    args = ["--runner", "pooling", "--enforce-eager", "--max-num-seqs", "5"]
+    text = "a photo of a cat"
+
+    with RemoteOpenAIServer(dual_encoder_model, args) as server:
+
+        def embed(payload: dict) -> EmbeddingResponse:
+            response = requests.post(
+                server.url_for("v1/embeddings"),
+                json={"model": dual_encoder_model, **payload},
+            )
+            response.raise_for_status()
+            return EmbeddingResponse.model_validate(response.json())
+
+        def user_message(part: dict) -> dict:
+            return {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [part]}]}
+
+        from_image = embed(
+            user_message({"type": "image_url", "image_url": image_base64})
+        )
+        from_input = embed({"input": text})
+        from_messages = embed(user_message({"type": "text", "text": text}))
+
+    assert from_image.usage.prompt_tokens == 1
+    assert from_messages.usage.prompt_tokens == from_input.usage.prompt_tokens
+    check_embeddings_close(
+        embeddings_0_lst=float_embeddings(from_input),
+        embeddings_1_lst=float_embeddings(from_messages),
+        name_0="input",
+        name_1="messages",
+    )
